Introduction of MPLADS 
*401. SHRI MANOJ BHATTACHARYA:††
 SHRI N.K. PREMACHANDRAN: 
Will  the  Minister  of  STATISTICS AND   PROGRAMME 
LEMENTATION be pleased to state: 
(a) since when the MPLADS has been in place; 
(b) the purpose for which the scheme was introduced: 
(c) whether any survey has been made to assess the efficacy of the 
erne; 
(d) if so, the results thereof; and 
(e) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF STATISTICS ID 
PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION (SHRI OSCAR FERNANDES): to (e) 
A statement is laid on the table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) The Member of Parliament Lo cal Area Development Scheme 
IPLADS) has been in place since 23rd December, 1993. 
(b) The purpose of the MPLAD Scheme  is to enable Members of 
iriiament to recommend works of developmental nature in their 
nstituencies with emphasis on creation of durable assets based on ;ally felt 
needs. 
(c) The Programme Evaluation Organisation of the Planning mmission 
conducted a study on the MPLADS implementation during 94-95 to 1998-99 
through sample survey in the structure schedules om 22 State Nodal 
Departments, 92 Lok Sabha MPs, 25 Rajya Sabha 
† The question was actually asked on the floor of the House by Shri Manoj 
Bhattacharya. 
 
1

RAJYA SABHA [21 April, 2005] 
MPs, 103 District Collectors, 590 development functionaries, 590 villagers/ urban persons and 
2892 local people. The report was finalized in November, 2001. 
(d) and (e) Some of the important suggestions given in the Report ' are as follows: 
(i) Adequate arrangements need to made for making all relevant information available to 
the Member of Parliament, (ii) The State Nodal Departments should be strengthened in 
terms of staff and other infrastructure, (iii) At the grass root level, the Panchayat Raj 
Institutions may be involved in execution as well as in monitoring to a larger extent, (iv) 
The Panchayat Raj Institutions may be asked to provide a list of works to be 
recommended to the MP annually and to help them to draw up priority list of works, (v) It 
may be appropriate to think in terms of coordination of works recommended under Member 
of Legislative Assembly Local Area Development (MLALAD) Scheme together with 
those recommended for the respective Lok Sabha Constituencies and utilize them in a 
more fruitful way without interfering with the freedom of individual MPs and MLAs to 
recommend work of their choice within their budgetary limits, (vi) The MP may consider 
allocation of fund only after the cost estimates is prepared and detailed work plan and 
coordination mechanism are made available to him. (vii) Since engaging contractors and 
payment of contingency charges cannot be avoided for pragmatic reasons, the 
Guidelines may be amended accordingly and prescise procedures specified for this 
purpose, (viii) It is necessary to locate an agency to maintain the assets before the issue of 
sanction, (ix) In order to overcome the problem of rising unspent balance in the districts, the 
report suggested that the funding of MPLADS should be a lapsable. (x) Details of MPLADS 
work should be compulsorily displayed at the site.

Karnataka, have been targeted, that is targeted to particular clouds and perhaps, on that

such a procedure what we have to do is to have sufficient number of rain gauges in areas where 
precipitation had not taken place so that, in comparison to the results in areas where 
precipitation has taken place we can come to the conclusion that rainfall was on account

validation of precipitation, it is impossible for us to say that the experiment of targeted cloud

Indian territory in illegal occupation of Pakistan and China 
3152. SHRI C. PERUMAL: Will the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS

China and Pakistan; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EXTERNAL 
AFFAIRS (SHR) E. AHAMMED): (a) to (c) India has outstanding boundary 
issues to be resolved with Pakistan and China. Pakistan has been in illegal and 
forcible occupation of approximately 78,000 sq. kms. of Indian territory. 
China continues to be in illegal occupation of approximately 38,000 sq. kms. 
in the Indian State of Jammu and Kashmir. In addition, under the so-called "Sino-
Pakistan Boundary Agreement of 1963", Pakistan illegally ceded 5180 sq. kms. of 
Indian territory in Pakistan Occupied Kashmir to China.

territory in the eastern Sector of India-China boundary in Arunachal Pradesh. 
India and Pakistan are committed under Shimla agreement and as 
reiterated in the Lahore declaration to resolve outstanding issues peacefully 
through bilateral dialogue.  
India and China seek a fair, r easonable and mutually acceptable 
settlement of the boundary question th rough peaceful consultations. In the 
Declaration of Principles for Relations and Comprehensive Cooperation issued on June 
23,2003, India and China have agreed to each appoint a Special Representative to 
explore from the political perspective of the overall bilateral relationship, the 
framework of a boundary settlement. Five meetings have been held so far between 
the Special Representatives of the two side.

Safety of Women Workers 
3176. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the Minister of LABOUR AND 
EMPLOYMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government propose to allow women to work in late-night 
shifts; 
(b) if so, whether Government have taken into consideration the negative 
health impact on women working in late-night shifts, as per study conducted in 
various foreign countries; 
(c) if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether working in night shift increases a women's risk of 
developing breast cancer and other cancers and that night shift has the strongest 
indication of negative effect on pregnancy; and 
(e) if so, whether Government would review its decision for the health and 
safety of women workers? 
THE MINISTER OF LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT .(SHRI K. 
CHANDRASEKHAR RAO): (a) On the demands of the Women's 
Organization and keeping in view the spirit of the International Labour 
Organization Protocol of 1990 to the Night Work (Women) Convention 
(Revised), 1948 and the present economic globalization, it has been decided to amend 
Section 66 of the Factories Act, 1948 to allow employment of women workers 
between 7.00 P.M. and 6.00 A.M. The Bill for the proposed amendment inter-alia 
provide that the occupier has to ensure occuptional safety and adequate 
protection of the women workers so employed by him. 
(b) to (d) Some studies are reported to have associated shift work and 
night work in particular with sleep difficulties and other medical disorders including 
increasing risk of developing breast cancer. However, majority of developed 
countries are found to permit the nigh t shift by women because there is no 
published evidence for any such condition to be regarded as an absolute reason to 
exclude them from shift work. 
(e) Does notarise.

Courts under Article 226/227 shall cont inue even after the setting up of the

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL): (a) Based on the seismological, 
geological, geotechnical, geophysical, engineering and other relevant 
scientific inputs, the country has been divided into four seismic zones, namely 
Zone II, II, IV and V. Zone V is considered to be most seismically active, while 
Zone II is the least. Seismic Zone V broadly comprises of entire north-eastern 
India, parts of Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttaranchal, Rann of Kutch 
in Gujarat, parts of north Bihar and Andaman and Nicobar Islands. Zone IV covers 
remaining parts of Jammu and Kashmir and Himachal Pradesh, Union Territory of 
Delhi, Sikkim, northern parts of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal, parts of 
Gujarat and a portion of Maharashtra and Rajasthan. 
(b) The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) has published-various 
guidelines and codes for design and construction of earthquake resistant 
structures, as well as retrofitting of build ings etc. Losses due to earthquakes 
can considerably be reduced if these guidelines/codes are followed during new 
constructions/strengthening of existing structures etc.

Maritime Policy 
3204. SHRI RAVI SHANKAR PRASAD: 
SHRI B.J. PANDA: 
Will  the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government hae formulated a maritime policy 
to secure rail, road and inland waterway connectivity; 
(b) if so, the broad details of the policy; 
(c) the action plan of Government for the construction of dedicated rail lines 
for freight movement from and to ports with special reference to Paradip? 
THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND 
HIGHWAYS (SHRI T.R. BAALU): (a) and (b) A comprehensive policy for the 
Maritime Sector which includes Ports, Merchant Shipping and Inland Water 
Transport (IWT) is under finalization. The policy seeks to combine vision and 
strategy for the sector through harmonious and coordinated development of 
our maritime assets like ports, shipping, inland water transport systems and ship 
building and ship repair industries. The following objectives are sought to be 
realized under the policy:— 
(i) Holistic development of maritime transport systems through a 
coordinated plan and strategies for development of port infrastructure, 
improvement in shipping, backward integration of the hinterland 
through rail, road and inland water transport connectivity, 
augmentation of ship building and ship repair facilities so as to emerge as an 
internationally competitive nation in this area by 2025. 
(ii) Ensure quality service comparable with international benchmarks in 
Indian ports through modernization, improvement in productivity and 
structural reforms. 
159 

RAJYA SABHA [21 April, 2005] 
(iii) Facilitate transhipment of Indian origin/bound cargo in Indian ports. 
(iv) Effect significant increase in  Indian Shipping and IWT tonnage 
through facilitative policy interventions. 
(v) Promote coastal shipping and inland water transport through a 
package of measures including fiscal and financial incentives. 
(vi) Strengthen maritime administration and bring about regulatory 
framework reforms to promote good governance. 
(vii) Provide level playing field to Indian stakeholders by providing fiscal 
regime at par with international norms and by rationalizing domestic 
levies. 
(viii) Provide for state-of-the-art aids to navigation,and requisite 
regulatory framework. 
(ix) Encourage ship-building and ship-repair activities to become 
internationally competitive and emerge as a leading ship-building/ ship-
repair nation by 2025. 
(x) Support ship-breaking and ship-recycling activities without 
compromising on environmental concerns. 
(xi) Stimulate private sector investment including foreign direct 
investment particularly for rendering services of a commercial nature 
in the Maritime sector, by providing conducive environment. 
(xii) Promote shipping-trade interface by evolving code of conduct for 
supply chain players such as freight forwarders, shipping agents, 
multimodal transport operators and other intermediaries. 
(xiii) Develop human resources in maritime sector and market them in the 
context of emerging global shortage of qualified personnel in the 
sector. 
(c) Setting up of National Dedicated Freight Rail Corridor from Northern Indian 
hinterland to Southern India which would be linked with the various ports is 
invisaged in the draft policy for the Maritime Sector (Ports, Merchant Shipping and 
Inland Water Transport). The draft policy further envisages that the corridor 
would be operated in the private sector and would have its own rolling stock, 
locomotives, signaling system, stations etc. but will follow the standards laid 
down by the Railways. The policy is at draft 
160 

[21 April, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
stage and would need the approval of the competent authority before being 
operationalised. 
For Paradip Port, presently the Cuttack—Paradip single rail line 
provides the sole link between Paradip Port and its hinterland. Work on 
doubling of this rail line in three reaches namely, (i) Nergundi — Cuttack 
Raghunathpur, (ii) Raghunathpur — Rahama & (iii) Rahama — Paradip 
Sections, has already ben taken up. The Railways has further taken up 
construction of the Daitari — Banspani  rail line for transport of iron ore 
traffic at Paradip Port. Haridaspur — Paradip rail link which is a virtual 
extension of the Daitari Banspani new rail link which will connect the iron ore 
rich belt of Banspani and Daitari sectors to Paradip Port is also under 
consideration.

Freight rail corridors 
3221. SHRI ANAND SHARMA: Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD 
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government propose to set up dedicated freight rail 
corridors to connect ports with the hinterland; 
(b) if so, the details of the proposed policy and target year of 
completion; and 
(c) the other steps proposed for the revamp of the maritime sector? 
THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND 
HIGHWAYS (SHRI T.R. BAALU): (a ) and (b) Setting up of National 
Dedicated Freight Rail Corridor from the hinterland of Northern part of India to 
Southern part of India which would be linked with the various ports is 
envisaged in the draft policy for the Maritime Sector (Ports, Merchant 
Shipping and Inland Water Transport). The draft policy further envisages that the 
corridor would be operated in the private sector and would have its own rolling 
stock, locomotives, signaling system, stations etc. but will follow the standards 
laid down by the Railways. The policy would need the approval of the 
competent authority. 
(c) There is no proposal for revamping the maritime sector per se. 
However, development and modernization of the maritime sector, which 
includes Ports, Merchant Shipping and Inland Water Transport (IWT), are 
undertaken as part of the on-going process, to cope with the demands of maritime 
trade. During the Tenth Five Year Plan period, an amount of Rs. 14220 Crores 
has been allocated for development of the maritime sector. Apart from the 
above, an investment of Rs. 11257 Crores by the private sector is also 
envisaged in major ports during the Tenth Plan period. Various measures 
aimed at creation of additional cargo handling capacities in the ports to reduce 
waiting time for ships calling at these ports, deepening of channels to 
facilitate berthing If large size vessels, improving road and rail connectivity to 
hinterland, augmentation of the shipping fleet, promotion of coastal shipping, 
modernization of navigational aids, encouragement of Indian ship building 
industry to make it globally competitive, development of inland water 
transport infrastructure so as to increase the share of inland cargo movement etc. 
have been/are being undertaken.

camera system providing 2.5m spatial resolution. A micro-satellite for

with Cartosat-1.

capability at 1m spatial resolution.

3242. SHRI N.R. GOVINDRAJAR: Will the Minister of YOUTH 
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether India's performance in various international sports events has 
been poor; and

the performance particularly in the forthcoming Olympic and Commonwealth 
games? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI SUNIL 
DUTT): (a) The performance of Indian sportspersons at major international events 
is steadily improving as indicated hereunder:— 
— In XXVIII Olympic Games, 2004 he ld at Athens, Greece, India won 
the first silver medal in individual event (Double Trap shooting) since 
independence. 
— In XII Paralympic Games, 2004, held at Athens, Greece, India won 
one gold medal (Javelin) and one silver medal (Power lifting). 
— In XVII Commonwealth Games, 2002 held at Manchester, U.K. India 
won 69 Medals (30 Gold, 22 Silver and 17 bronze) and secured 4th 
position. 
— In XIV Asian Games, 2002 held at Busan, South Korea India won 36 
Medals (11 Gold, 12 Silver and 13 Bronze) and secured 7th Position. 
— In 1st Afro-Asian Games, 2003 held at Hyderabad India secure 80 
medals (19 Gold, 32 Silver and 29 Bronze) and secured 2nd Position.

— In the SAF Games, 2004 held at Islamabad, Pakistan India secured 
191 Medals (101 Gold, 59 Silver and 31 Bronze) and secured 1st 
position.

National Sports Federations. Government of India, in addition to providing sports 
infrastructure, under Sports Authority of lndia (SAI) is taking the following 
steps to improve the performance of sportspersons in the international 
games:—

(LTDPs) for various sports disciplines in consultation with the 
concerned National Sports Federations, former international 
sportspersons and sports/scientists experts.

coaching camps.

sportspersons in international tournaments.

can have nutritious diet, sports equipment support and be able to 
pursue sports as a career. Scholarships are also given for research in

and participation within the country and abroad is proved under the 
'Scheme relating to Talent Search and Training' and the 'National 
Sports Development Fund'.

non-receipt of adequate help from the Mini stry of Sports, SAI are not able to 
hold fresh trails for the Bulgarian Wrestling Meet;

wrestlers had fled the National Camp at Aurangabad Special Training Centre 
alleging poor living conditions, etc;

(d) the steps taken to ensure that Sports Training Institute and similar 
training-oriented organisation have world-class training inputs and matching 
infrastructure facilities? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI SUNIL 
DUTT): (a) No, Sir. the selection trials are conducted by the concerned 
National Sports Federation (NSF) i.e. Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) in this 
case. WFI conducted two trails for this meet on 5th March & 19th March, 
2005, respectively.

facilities and bad treatment. The Director General, Sports Authority of India, who 
was deputed to conduct an inquiry, reported that the playing facilities as well as

satisfactory. As per information received from SAI, 37 wrestlers in the camp, 
alongwith 24 unauthorized persons staying with the campers at Aurangabad 
left the camp on 1st March, 2005 because the presence of 24 extra persons was 
objected to by the senior coach of the Sports Authority of India. The wrestlers 
later went back & joined the camp.

Demand to Include Tourism in the Concurrent List of the Constitution 
SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY SIRIGIRE DDY (Andhra Pradesh): Sir, India 
is blessed by its diversity, natural beauty, culture and heritage. Not only this, 
the seasonal benefits can also make India a potential year-round tourist 
destination of the world. In spite of  having these God-gifted advantages, the 
trourism industry is not able to exploit t he situation. One of the main problems 
is that tourism industry in India does not have a single global voice, and there 
is a lack of collective effort from both,  the private sector and the Government 
of India, to achieve its latent potential. The reason for this is that Governments 
at State and Central levels are not able to  have uniform legislation for getting 
the desired results. The reason bein g Tourism'—as per the division of 
legislative powers between the States and the Union, as stipulated under 
Article 248 of the Constitution—is not included either in the State List or the 
Union List or even in the Concurrent List of the Seventh Schedule of the 
Constitution. So, this arrangement has been causing a lot of problem. Some 
time back, a proposal was mooted to include Tourism' in the Concurrent List, 
to give Constitutional recognition to tourism sector, and to help channelising 
development of tourism in a systematic way. The proposal was circulated to all 
the States/ Union Territories. I understan d that 29 States/Union Territories 
have agreed to include Tourism' in the Concurrent List, hence, I request the 
Government of India that since maximu m States have agreed to the proposal 
and looking at the potential of tourism, employment ge neration, revenue, etc. 
to immediately include Tourism' in the Concurrent List, without further delay.

SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA (Rajasthan):  Sir, I rise to commend this

notifications without surveying their vegetation or ecological status and settling 
the rights of pre-existing occupants.

ferociously rebel against forest destr uction by the States and commercial 
interests. In Orissa and Jharkhand, thousands of villages are regenerating and 
protecting the forests on their own, simply because their lives and livelihood

SHRI B.J. PANDA(Orissa): Orissa has around 32,000 hectares of 
potential brackish water area for development of aquaculture. It has been gifted

demand abroad. In view of this potential, MPEDA has submitted a mission mode

shrimp and 10,000 hectares of scampi farms. As the Government is aware, Orissa is 
a debt-ridden cash strapped State, and it cannot afford to make provision even 
for Rs. 673 crores, whereas much more money is required for the purpose. 
The State has to create necessary infrastructure, impart training to the farmers 
and remove the unnecessary bottlenecks. This is not possible without adequate 
Central financial assistance to the State. 
I would, therefore, request the Centre to release adequate Central 
assistance to the State for tapping this potential to help the State improve its 
economy.
